subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should OpenClaw treat the LiteLLM/Vertex beta generic 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` shape as a recoverable provider/session request-shape error, and if so which owner boundary should implement it?
rationale: Current source shows the gap, but generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` can mean several provider-side problems, so choosing provider-owned classification, context/fallback recovery, or only diagnostic copy needs maintainer intent and live provider evidence.

options.title: Provider-scoped recovery
options.body: Add a LiteLLM/Vertex-scoped classifier or plugin hook for the verified shape, with redacted logging, actionable user copy, and session-lane proof.

options.title: Diagnostics only until live proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a live Vertex beta repro before changing recovery behavior beyond better logs and copy.

options.title: Fold into generic recovery
options.body: Treat broader generic provider `INVALID_ARGUMENT` failures as conversation-state recovery candidates, accepting higher misclassification risk.

recommendation.title: Provider-scoped recovery
recommendation.body: Add a LiteLLM/Vertex-scoped classifier or plugin hook for the verified shape, with redacted logging, actionable user copy, and session-lane proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the adjacent provider failover normalization work and are the best available history-backed route for deciding provider recovery semantics.
